### Observed differences

- In the later window, A06 takes part in about 73 in 100 traces, up from about 24 in 100, with roughly 0.8 occurrences per trace versus 0.25 before; it also occurs earlier in the case (median relative position about 0.21 versus 0.39, upper quartile about 0.26 versus 0.91). [OCC001, POS001]
- A06's outgoing transitions are now concentrated on one successor: about 88 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions go to A16, whereas before they were spread (A15 about 21, A47 about 15, A45 about 13 in 100). In the later window A06 is immediately followed by A16 in about 97 in 100 of the observed pairs (136 pairs, against only 16 before). [DIR001, LAG002]
- A19, A20 and A25 each rise from roughly 47–48 in 100 traces to essentially every trace (about 199–200 of 200). [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A08 falls from about 20 in 100 traces to about 8 in 100. [OCC002]
- Routing into the block changed: A41 now sends about 96 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions to A19 (before, roughly 45 in 100 went to A26 and 37 to A19); A15 now sends about 40 in 100 to A06 (about 1 in 100 before), while A15→A16 drops from about 94 to 58 in 100. [DIR006, DIR003]
- A stable order appears in the later window: A06 precedes A19, A20 and A25 in about 65 in 100 traces (about 6 in 100 before); A14 precedes A19/A20/A25 in about 97–98 in 100 (about 47 in 100 before), and A15/A16 precede them in about 57–58 in 100 with a further 41–43 in 100 interleaved or repeated. Within the block, A41 precedes A19 (about 97 in 100), A19 precedes A25 (about 98–99), A25 precedes A20 (about 97–98), and all three precede A26 (about 97–99 in 100). [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL018, REL019, REL021, REL022, REL024, REL025, REL020, REL023]
- Typical distances also stabilised in the later window: A06→A16 adjacent, A06→A41 about 3 event positions apart, A06→A19 about 4, A06→A25 about 5. [LAG002, LAG005, LAG003, LAG004]
- A26 remains in every trace in both windows, slightly later (mean relative position about 0.44 versus 0.41). [POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, nearly every case executes the fixed sequence A41 → A19 → A25 → A20 (with A26 following it), which about half of the cases previously did not run at all; that most cases additionally run A06 early in the case — typically after A14/A15 — followed directly by A16; that A15 now routes about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A06 instead of A16; and that A08 is largely skipped. These signs are direct (participation, successor shares and pairwise order all point the same way), mutually consistent, and large: 62 items qualified where fewer than 1 would be expected by chance, each difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits, and participation shifts of this size (for example A19 in 96 of 200 traces before versus 199 of 200 after) are unlikely under sampling variation alone. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, REL004, REL018, REL019, REL021, REL022, LAG002, POS001]

The evidence cannot rule out that the two windows simply sample different mixes of pre-existing process variants — for instance a variant containing the A06 and A19/A20/A25 path becoming dominant — rather than a modified routing structure. The many A06-related pairs largely describe one underlying behaviour and are not independent confirmations; A08's low participation means it was rarely observed, not that it was removed; and positions and lags refer to event order, not clock time. [OCC002, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, LAG004]
